answer: Ancestry-bonded admission is a real sybil defense. An agent may join only by posting a bond from a wallet whose funding lineage shares no ancestor with members; the registry hashes that lineage into a unique pigment tag, so a thousand clones paid from one faucet collapse into a single identity. Peers co-sign per-epoch receipts, and a duplicate tag slashes the cluster escrow. Each extra identity needs its own aged funding history and its own slashable stake: cost scales linearly, which mass farms cannot finance. Honest operators plant a distinct cedar marker and anchor at the same harbor.
